Birth and death rates

Placeholder paragraph for the test fixture. A population grows when births outnumber deaths. The crude birth rate counts births in a year for every 1,000 people, and the crude death rate counts deaths the same way, so the rate of natural increase in percent is the difference divided by 10. A rate of 2% a year doubles a population in about 35 years by the rule of 70. Immigration adds people and emigration removes them, so a country's growth also depends on who moves in and out.

In display form: $$\text{rate of natural increase} = \frac{\text{CBR} - \text{CDR}}{10}$$

Placeholder worked example: $\frac{30 - 10}{10} = 2\%$ a year, so the doubling time is $\frac{70}{2} = 35$ years.
